task.title: Review and fix a buggy Java order-service method
task.brief: Below is a short Java method from an order service. It should remove cancelled orders and return the average order value for one city, but it crashes sometimes and gives wrong numbers. In 20 to 25 minutes: (1) list each bug or risk and explain what goes wrong at run time, (2) write a corrected version of the method, and (3) say how you would test it (a few cases with expected results). No code is run, so explain your reasoning.
key_points: Removing from the list inside a for-each throws ConcurrentModificationException; use removeIf or an Iterator
o.getCity() can be null, causing NullPointerException; use cityFilter.equals(o.getCity()) or Objects.equals
Average divides by all orders, not by the number of orders in the city
Integer division drops paise; cast to double or use BigDecimal
Division by zero / empty list when no orders match must be handled
Suggests tests: no orders, all cancelled, null city, mixed cities with a known average

rubric.label: Bugs found and fixed
rubric.guide: 0 = finds none or fix still wrong, 3 = finds two or three main bugs, 5 = finds string compare, list removal, null city, wrong divisor and integer division, all fixed

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.guide: 0 = none mentioned, 3 = some, 5 = handles empty list, no match, null values and all-cancelled orders with tests

rubric.label: Explanation
rubric.guide: 0 = no reasons, 3 = reasons thin or partly wrong, 5 = each bug explained clearly with what happens at run time

rubric.label: Code quality
rubric.guide: 0 = new bugs or unreadable, 3 = works but clumsy, 5 = clean, idiomatic Java (removeIf, streams or clear loops)
